context_requirements: Active DNA/histone methylation machinery (DNMT1, DNMT3A, EZH2) for inhibitor engagement
Intact p53 pathway for robust CDKN1A induction and DNA-damage response
Proliferating cells for antiproliferative and cell-cycle transcriptional effects
falsifiers: No change in CDKN1A, TXNIP, or DNMT1/DNMT3A/EZH2 expression at 6 or 24 h in any responsive line
Strong and selective upregulation of PPARG target genes without any methylation-related or antiproliferative signature
No difference in magnitude between 6 h and 24 h across all nine lines, contradicting slow kinetics
Absence of any proliferation_down or DNA-damage-response signature at 24 h in lines with known p53 function

evidence.supports: DNA methyltransferase inhibition induces immunomodulatory and interferon-related gene expression in epithelial cancer lines
Histone methyltransferase inhibition upregulates TXNIP, increases ROS, and induces ER-stress and apoptosis signatures
DNA methyltransferase inhibition induces DNA double-strand break responses, p53 activation, and apoptosis
DNA methyltransferase inhibition produces limited, conserved gene expression changes including proliferation and immune-presentation genes
DNMT inhibition increases p21 and decreases cyclin D, causing S-phase arrest in breast cancer lines

changes: Replaced primary_targets PPARG with DNMT1, DNMT3A, EZH2, which are the direct targets of methyltransferase inhibitors; PPARG is not a methyltransferase.
Removed PPARG from context_requirements because it is not the direct target of this mechanism class.
